newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Supreme Court ruled yesterday that there is yet no law to amend the term limits of elective officials and other provisions in the Constitution through a people's initiative. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- President Ramos yesterday said the government decision to provide temporary shelter to North Korean defector Hwang Jang Yop was in line with its policy to help bring peace and stability in the region. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Commission on Appointment yesterday bypassed for the sixth time Transportation and Communications Secretary Amado Lagdameo amid calls for his resignation from the Cabinet. (INQUIRER)
- The country's balance of payments in the first two months of 1997 yielded a surplus of $463.8 million, down by 40 percent from the $769.2 million posted in the same period in 1996. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Internal problems hounding the Philippine Stock Exchange are making foreign fund managers apprehensive about the capability of the privately-run bourse to operate professionally. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- A battle for corporate control is said to be brewing at A. Soriano Corp, the holding company for the Soriano family's diverse commercial and financial interests. (TIMES/INQUIRER)
